claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace establishes the deviation. It measures the trip at 7.89 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a platform optimal of 6.20 km, an excess of 1.69 km, or 27.26% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are passed: the excess is greater than 0.80 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not trip_record.actual_distance_km, which is a rounded convenience copy (7.90 km) and may not be cited for the threshold test.

The trace needs no corroboration and nothing about it is in doubt. It carries 121 fixes over a 20-minute trip at a 10-second sample interval, with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. It therefore fails none of the impairment limbs POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and the independent-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) is not engaged. A deviation may be established on this trace alone.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges both limbs of it. The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00518 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and their timestamps are consistent (requested 08:20:00, accepted 08:20:40, first fix 08:26:40, charged 08:47:00), with no disagreement approaching the 10-minute mark. The excess of 1.69 km / 27.26% is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's only explanation is that the road 'avoids two junctions' and is 'a real shortcut when the main road is busy'. That is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00518-01, is MISSING: it has no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. The chat_log for this trip is empty: message_count is 0, the message array is empty and first_message_at and last_message_at are null. There is therefore no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor and none within three minutes after, and POL-RD-04 fails at its first requirement. The driver does not assert in his statement that the rider asked for the route.

Nor was either endpoint moved, so the baseline is not re-quoted. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null. POL-RD-05 has no work to do, and the booked optimal of 6.20 km stands as the measure of excess.

The remedy is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and none of the clauses that would displace it applies. The fare_breakdown records fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote route is closed, and the trip_record records vehicle_type RYDE_TAXI and a null solo_optimal_distance_km, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The excess is not exonerated under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04 or POL-RD-05, so the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic runs as follows, and I give the figures on separate lines as the clause requires. charged_total = 16.13. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.20 + 0.28 x 10.50) x the surge_multiplier recorded on the FARE_BREAKDOWN, which is 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19; there is no ERP or toll gantry on the optimal route, no airport surcharge, a waiting_time_fee of 0.00 and a promo_discount of 0.00 to add. Refund = 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, and the payable figure is rounded UP to SGD 3.95. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is payable rather than dismissed; at 24.43% of charged_total it does not reach the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

There is no pass-through correction to add on top, and none to deduct either: the fare_breakdown carries no erp_gantries, tolls_erp of 0.00, airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and no unmatched charge line. POL-RD-09 therefore neither enlarges nor reduces the POL-RD-02 figure, and the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) is satisfied because the 3.95 refund is charged_total less a recomputed fare containing no off-route gantries.

The present state of the ledger matters to the ruling value. The fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so although the rider recalls that the app 'refunded the difference immediately', the disputed charge stands on the record and I do not rely on that recollection. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves exactly that state as it is, which on a rider-filed dispute means the rider keeps carrying the whole 16.13. Only a refund under POL-RD-02 moves money back.

No escalation trigger fires, and the case should be decided on the money rather than held. The identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so POL-RD-10(2) is not engaged; the trace is unimpaired, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, so POL-RD-13(1) keeps the absent advisory out of POL-RD-10(5) - an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one; and the computed refund of 3.95 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6).

Nothing on the rider's profile adds a hurdle. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the 4-claim threshold in POL-RD-08, so the additional corroboration requirement in that clause is not triggered and could not be used in any event to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. No other field on the rider profile may ground anything: under POL-GEN-01 the counters not named in a clause are context only.

No traffic advisory covers this trip, and the driver has cited none. EV-ADVIS-00518-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, an admissibility weight_multiplier of 0.0, and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's passing reference to a busier main road is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, so it buys him no exoneration under POL-RD-03. But because neither party has named an advisory identifier, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it is expressly NOT a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger. The case can and should be decided on the arithmetic rather than held, so no terminal ESCALATE should issue.

Even on the rider's own derived figures the deviation is established but not MATERIAL. The excess is 1.69 km, 27.26 percent of the 6.2 km optimal — below both the 8.0 km and the 50 percent materiality gates of POL-RD-01 — so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip. The driver's profile bears that out: 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 250 completed trips, nowhere near the 3-flag or 5 percent-of-40 pattern test. There is therefore no licence for a FULL_REFUND uplift and no basis for a driver-conduct referral.

The rider has been billed the metered distance she was actually driven through, and no more. On this METERED fare the POL-RD-02 recomputation is (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.2 + 0.28 x 10.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19. The most any distance refund can therefore be is 16.13 - 12.19, approximately SGD 3.94 rounded up to SGD 3.95 — roughly a quarter of the fare, not the SGD 16.13 the dispute names, and far short of the 90 percent share that would convert a partial into a FULL_REFUND.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity element in this fare at all. The fare_breakdown carries erp_gantries [], tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, and the billed distance of 7.9 km matches the trace's 7.89 km essentially to the metre. There is no off-route ERP to add on top of any distance figure (POL-RD-09(1)) and no unmatched or phantom line to refer under POL-RD-09(4).

The claim text's assertion that the app 'refunded the difference immediately' is not borne out by the record: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The present state therefore still stands in the driver's favour, and under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION outcome leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are — it never restores or increases a charge, but equally it strips nothing from the driver that has not been ordered.

The call the rider now emphasises was an in-app platform call: the trip record shows one call, placed by the DRIVER, answered, lasting 190 seconds, routed through the app. No private telephone number of the rider's was exposed by it. It is not a fare matter — none of the ruling values defined in POL-GEN-03 provides a remedy for it — and a conduct referral is available only under POL-RD-06(c) on an established repeat pattern, which the driver's 0 flags in 90 days does not supply.

THE TRACE IS CLEAN. EV-GPS-00518 carries 121 fixes over the 20-minute trip at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s. The bundle holds one advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00518-01, and it is MISSING: no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-11 (upfront fares) is closed because the fare model is METERED, and POL-RD-12 (pooled trips) does not apply because the vehicle is RYDE_TAXI with a null solo optimal.

THE REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02), read off the fare breakdown EV-FARE-00518:
  charged_total = 16.13
  recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.20 + 0.28 x 10.50) x 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19
  refund = 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, rounded UP to SGD 3.95.
There is no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge line (all 0.00, erp_gantries empty), a waiting_time_fee of 0.00 and a promo_discount of 0.00, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and deducts nothing, and there is no phantom or unmatched line to refer as a billing-integrity finding. The refund of 3.95 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is payable rather than dismissed, and at 24.4% of the charged total it does not reach the 90% share that would convert the outcome to a full refund. The outcome is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.95.

PRESENT STATE OF THE LEDGER. The rider recalls that the app 'refunded the difference immediately'. The record does not bear that out: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. That is exactly the state a NO_ACTION ruling would leave, and it is the state this ruling changes — the 3.95 above is the money that moves.

THE POST-TRIP CALL. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00518) shows the only call was a single in-app platform call, placed by the driver after the trip, answered, lasting 190 seconds, routed through the app. No private telephone number was exposed by it. No clause in this category provides a fare remedy or a mandated referral for it, so it produces no referral and no separate payment, and it does not affect the amount above. If the rider still wishes the contact to be looked at, that is a conduct matter for the platform's conduct team and it is recorded here as an open question; it is not a clause-mandated referral and I do not create one.

CONFIDENCE. The facts that decide this case are carried by EV-GPS-00518, EV-TRIP-00518 and EV-FARE-00518, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; I have set confidence at 0.95. The MISSING advisory at weight 0.0 carries no deciding fact and does not lower the cap.

The excess is 1.69 km, or 27.26% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (over 0.80 km and over 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 8.0 km and below 50%), so the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check is not engaged; the driver profile shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 250 completed trips, and no conduct referral follows from it. The trace itself is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): 121 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s, so no independent corroboration is required. Nothing on the rider profile adds a hurdle (deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4). Burden is discharged: identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown and timestamps are consistent.

No excuse reduces the excess. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00518) is empty, so there was no rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04). No endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05). The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00518-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the driver's explanation that the road 'avoids two junctions' is a traffic excuse tested against an advisory and nothing else (POL-RD-13), so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and buys no exoneration under POL-RD-03. Because no party cited an advisory identifier, its absence is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger, so the case is decided on the arithmetic and is not held.

The fare (EV-FARE-00518, weight 1.0) is METERED, so the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs. charged_total = 16.13; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.20 + 0.28 x 10.50) x the surge_multiplier read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN, which is 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19; refund = 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, rounded UP to 3.95. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and below 90% of the fare, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.95, not the SGD 16.13 named in the dispute. There is no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line (all 0.00), so POL-RD-09 neither adds nor subtracts: the 3.95 is not on top of any pass-through correction, and no phantom line exists to refer. The driver is owed no compensation: he was billed 7.90 km against a 7.89 km trace, a shortfall of about 0.01 km, nowhere near the 1.0 km POL-RD-04 threshold.

On the ledger and the call: the fare record shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider's recollection of an immediate refund is not borne out; this ruling is what moves the money, and the charge stands until it does. The post-trip contact was an in-app platform call placed by the driver and answered for 190 seconds, not a call on a private number, so the record gives no support for a number exposure. That concern is not a fare matter, no clause in this category produces a referral for it, and it does not affect the amount; if the rider wants the platform to look at a driver calling about a fare dispute more than an hour after the trip, that is best raised through in-app support.

ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace establishes the deviation. It measures the trip at 7.89 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a platform optimal of 6.20 km, an excess of 1.69 km, or 27.26% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are passed: the excess is greater than 0.80 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not trip_record.actual_distance_km, which is a rounded convenience copy (7.90 km) and may not be cited for the threshold test.

The trace needs no corroboration and nothing about it is in doubt. It carries 121 fixes over a 20-minute trip at a 10-second sample interval, with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. It therefore fails none of the impairment limbs POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and the independent-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) is not engaged. A deviation may be established on this trace alone.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges both limbs of it. The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00518 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and their timestamps are consistent (requested 08:20:00, accepted 08:20:40, first fix 08:26:40, charged 08:47:00), with no disagreement approaching the 10-minute mark. The excess of 1.69 km / 27.26% is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's only explanation is that the road 'avoids two junctions' and is 'a real shortcut when the main road is busy'. That is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00518-01, is MISSING: it has no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. The chat_log for this trip is empty: message_count is 0, the message array is empty and first_message_at and last_message_at are null. There is therefore no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor and none within three minutes after, and POL-RD-04 fails at its first requirement. The driver does not assert in his statement that the rider asked for the route.

Nor was either endpoint moved, so the baseline is not re-quoted. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null. POL-RD-05 has no work to do, and the booked optimal of 6.20 km stands as the measure of excess.

The remedy is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and none of the clauses that would displace it applies. The fare_breakdown records fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote route is closed, and the trip_record records vehicle_type RYDE_TAXI and a null solo_optimal_distance_km, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The excess is not exonerated under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04 or POL-RD-05, so the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic runs as follows, and I give the figures on separate lines as the clause requires. charged_total = 16.13. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.20 + 0.28 x 10.50) x the surge_multiplier recorded on the FARE_BREAKDOWN, which is 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19; there is no ERP or toll gantry on the optimal route, no airport surcharge, a waiting_time_fee of 0.00 and a promo_discount of 0.00 to add. Refund = 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, and the payable figure is rounded UP to SGD 3.95. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is payable rather than dismissed; at 24.43% of charged_total it does not reach the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

There is no pass-through correction to add on top, and none to deduct either: the fare_breakdown carries no erp_gantries, tolls_erp of 0.00, airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and no unmatched charge line. POL-RD-09 therefore neither enlarges nor reduces the POL-RD-02 figure, and the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) is satisfied because the 3.95 refund is charged_total less a recomputed fare containing no off-route gantries.

The present state of the ledger matters to the ruling value. The fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so although the rider recalls that the app 'refunded the difference immediately', the disputed charge stands on the record and I do not rely on that recollection. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves exactly that state as it is, which on a rider-filed dispute means the rider keeps carrying the whole 16.13. Only a refund under POL-RD-02 moves money back.

No escalation trigger fires, and the case should be decided on the money rather than held. ledger.claim: Nothing on the rider's profile adds a hurdle. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the 4-claim threshold in POL-RD-08, so the additional corroboration requirement in that clause is not triggered and could not be used in any event to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. No other field on the rider profile may ground anything: under POL-GEN-01 the counters not named in a clause are context only.

No traffic advisory covers this trip, and the driver has cited none. EV-ADVIS-00518-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, an admissibility weight_multiplier of 0.0, and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's passing reference to a busier main road is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, so it buys him no exoneration under POL-RD-03. But because neither party has named an advisory identifier, the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it is expressly NOT a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger. The case can and should be decided on the arithmetic rather than held, so no terminal ESCALATE should issue.

Even on the rider's own derived figures the deviation is established but not MATERIAL. The excess is 1.69 km, 27.26 percent of the 6.2 km optimal — below both the 8.0 km and the 50 percent materiality gates of POL-RD-01 — so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip. The driver's profile bears that out: 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 250 completed trips, nowhere near the 3-flag or 5 percent-of-40 pattern test. There is therefore no licence for a FULL_REFUND uplift and no basis for a driver-conduct referral.

The rider has been billed the metered distance she was actually driven through, and no more. On this METERED fare the POL-RD-02 recomputation is (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.2 + 0.28 x 10.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19. The most any distance refund can therefore be is 16.13 - 12.19, approximately SGD 3.94 rounded up to SGD 3.95 — roughly a quarter of the fare, not the SGD 16.13 the dispute names, and far short of the 90 percent share that would convert a partial into a FULL_REFUND.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity element in this fare at all. The fare_breakdown carries erp_gantries [], tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, and the billed distance of 7.9 km matches the trace's 7.89 km essentially to the metre. There is no off-route ERP to add on top of any distance figure (POL-RD-09(1)) and no unmatched or phantom line to refer under POL-RD-09(4).

The claim text's assertion that the app 'refunded the difference immediately' is not borne out by the record: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The present state therefore still stands in the driver's favour, and under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION outcome leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are — it never restores or increases a charge, but equally it strips nothing from the driver that has not been ordered.

The call the rider now emphasises was an in-app platform call: the trip record shows one call, placed by the DRIVER, answered, lasting 190 seconds, routed through the app. No private telephone number of the rider's was exposed by it. It is not a fare matter — none of the ruling values defined in POL-GEN-03 provides a remedy for it — and a conduct referral is available only under POL-RD-06(c) on an established repeat pattern, which the driver's 0 flags in 90 days does not supply.
